title: 'Floating tractors' clean up weed-choked waterways

input.lead: Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 on a weed removal programme
input.summary: Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 on a weed removal programme
input.evidence_text: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause problems for boats The weeds can also starve underwater plants of light and reduce levels of oxygen needed by fish and other wildlife, and can have a damaging impact on kingfishers and otters Kieran Howlett, from the Canal & River Trust, said managing the weeds was becoming more challenging but the charity was determined to protect the "wonderful waterways" With warmer summers and longer growing seasons, these fast-growing plants spread quickly through the canal network and can rapidly form a thick green carpet across the water's surface Described as "a bit like floating tractors" by the Canal & River Trust, the specialist machines cut and collect weeds from the water, helping the team remove about 30 tonnes each week

title: Ryanair passenger describes 'traumatic' Murcia flight bomb threat

input.lead: Sarah Jones says passengers had to wait in a hangar for three hours after landing at Murcia in Spain
input.summary: Sarah Jones says passengers had to wait in a hangar for three hours after landing at Murcia in Spain
input.evidence_text: Ryanair passenger describes 'traumatic' Murcia flight bomb threat - BBC News Image source, Sarah Jones Image caption, Charlotte (left), Sarah and Kelly travelled to Spain to work as medics at a golf tournament By Haider Saleem North West Published 3 November 2026 The evacuation of a Ryanair aircraft after a suspected bomb threat has been described as "quite traumatic" by a passenger who was on board the flight. Sarah Jones said police, fire crews and bomb disposal officers surrounded the plane after it landed at Murcia airport from Manchester. The medic from Manchester said she and her fellow passengers were told to leave their belongings on board and then spent about three hours in an airport hangar while the plane was searched. Spanish officials said no explosives were found. The aircraft was one of seven searched at airports across Europe following a series of suspected bomb threats. Image source, Sarah Jones Image caption, Emergency services attended Murcia airport after the Ryanair aircraft landed Jones was travelling with colleagues Charlotte and Kelly to work as medics at a golf tournament in La Manga in south-eastern Spain. She said the flight was uneventful until the aircraft landed at about 10:30 local time (09:30 GMT). "When we landed, the plane just sort of stopped really quickly and we were held there for a while," she told the BBC. Passengers initially thought they were waiting for permission to taxi to the terminal. "Then we were just surrounded by police, the bomb squad, ambulances were there, fire engines," she said. "Then we were told that we needed to evacuate the plane, but we weren't allowed to bring anything off. "We had to leave the luggage in the overhead lockers." Image source, Sarah Jones Image caption, Passengers walked away from the aircraft

A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
